name: Spider (Solitaire)
description: Spider is one of the most popular two-deck solitaire games. The goal is to assemble 13 cards of a suit (K down to A) on the tableau, which then automatically removes itself from play. It is typically played with two decks (104 cards). The difficulty varies massively depending on the number of suits used (1 Suit = Easy, 2 Suits = Medium, 4 Suits = Hard).

history.origins: Spider is a type of patience game and one of the more popular two-deck solitaires. The game originated in 1949; its name comes from a spider's eight legs, referencing the eight foundation piles (complete King-to-Ace same-suit sequences) that must be removed to win. It was said to be a favorite of Franklin D. Roosevelt. Spider became widely known through Microsoft Plus! 98 for Windows 98 (1998) and remains a standard computerized solitaire.
timeline: Present: A standard on every PC.
history.cultural: Known for its 'impossible' deals in 4-Suit mode requiring undo or pure luck.
history.evolution: The 1-Suit variation was popularized by computers to make the game approachable.

setup.players: One player only. Spider is a solitaire (patience) game played by a single player against the tableau and stock.
setup.dealing: Deal 54 cards to the tableau in 10 columns: first 4 columns get 6 cards each, remaining 6 columns get 5 cards each; only the top card of each column is face up. The remaining 50 cards form the stock. When no column is empty, the player may deal 10 more cards from the stock (one to each column).
setup.equipment: Table space for 10 tableau columns and stock.

rules.objective: assemble 8 full sequences (K-Q-J...A) of the SAME SUIT.
rules.gameplay: Build down by rank on the tableau (any suit); in-suit sequences may be moved together. A complete run of 13 cards in one suit (King down to Ace) is removed from the tableau. When no column is empty, deal 10 cards from the stock (one per column). Continue until all eight sequences are removed (win) or no legal move and no deal remains (loss).
keyRules: Tableau builds down by rank; any suit.
In-suit sequences may be moved as a unit.
Complete K-to-A same suit is removed from play.
Deal 10 from stock only when no column is empty.

strategy.basic: Prioritize emptying piles to turn over face-down cards. An empty pile is goldâ€”it lets you move any junk card there to unblock others. In 2/4 Suit, try to keep piles 'pure' (same suit) as much as possible so you can move them later.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Tidy Up' Phase: Before dealing a new row, tidy up your runs. Make sure sequences are as consolidated as possible. If you have a choice between putting a 5-Hearts on a 6-Hearts or 6-Spades, choose Hearts.
strategy.advanced: Sacrificing a Run: Sometimes playing a 5-Hearts on a 6-Spades (blocking the run) is necessary to uncover a face-down card that might be a King. Uncovering cards > Maintaining runs.
tips: Don't fill an empty space with a King unless necessary.

variations.name: Spider 1 Suit
variations.description: Played with one suit only (usually Spades). Easiest variant; all cards are the same suit so any sequence can be moved.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation differs only by suit count; no engine constant overrides in schema for suit subset.

variations.name: Spider 2 Suit
variations.description: Played with two suits (usually Spades and Hearts). Medium difficulty; in-suit builds matter for moving sequences.

variations.description: Classic Spider with all four suits. Hardest variant; many deals are unwinnable without undo or luck.
